CITY_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS is `seo_indexable AND wikidata_qid IS NULL AND wikipedia_title IS NULL` (99991790194100:322), so all 11 became ambiguous the moment they stopped publishing another city's encyclopedia article. THE CEILING IS RAISED BECAUSE THE DATA CANNOT BE REPAIRED BACK UNDER IT: re-adding the identifiers republishes the wrong article, the correct QIDs are deliberately not guessed (prefer NULL to a guess), and city-factual-backfill's 100km coordinate guard now refuses re-adoption anyway. Those 11 rows are a human work list, not a regression. publication_blocked moves with it because 7 of the 11 had no other blocker (ready fell 1519 -> 1513 over the same window, net +6 after two unrelated image blockers cleared). Nothing renegotiated this at merge time because the repair was applied direct to prod and only reached the repo on 2026-09-26 in drift-recovery batch #3945, so it never passed a review where the live-data gate would have forced the contract change into the same diff.

THIS ONE IS NOT A BACKLOG AND THE ORIGINAL CEILING WAS MIS-SPECIFIED, not merely too low. `unlinked_events` is `count(*) from events where duplicate_of_id is null and city_id is null` (99991790194100:524) -- an INFLOW counter that rises with every ingested event whose city does not resolve and falls when run_event_city_link (cron `5 3 * * *`) drains it overnight. Measured across three consecutive daily snapshots it read 743 / 742 / 744, and the activation ceiling was pinned at the exact snapshot value with ZERO headroom, which makes it a coin flip that reds every open PR in the repo at random -- it did exactly that on 2026-09-26 when two events arrived with no resolvable city. The new ceiling is derived, not chosen: 744 currently unlinked + 90 days of the measured residue rate. Residue rate measured 2026-09-26 -- of the 744, only 12 were created in the trailing 30 days (0.4/day) while 727 came from a burst 30-90 days ago, so 0.4/day is normal accrual and 90 days of it is 36. A genuine producer regression is a step change of hundreds (that 727-event burst is the shape), so 36 of headroom still catches one while absorbing daily noise. `operations.unlinked_venues` carries the IDENTICAL defect and is green only by luck, because it happens to be falling (3584 -> 3534 -> 3518 over the same three snapshots); it is left alone here rather than pre-emptively loosened, but it is the same coin flip the day that trend reverses.

ONE BULK IMPORT MOVED FIVE COUNTERS AND RED EVERY OPEN PR IN THE REPO. On 2026-09-28 the gayout source landed 3,336 venues in a single day, every one WITH city text and a country_id (so drainable, not junk), plus 79 new `venue-city-match` city rows of which 33 are indexable. Nothing here is a producer regression and nothing can be repaired back under the old ceilings, so the ceilings move and each number below is DERIVED, not chosen. The two city-link zero-invariants that were red alongside these are NOT raised -- CITY_LINK_NAMESAKE and CITY_LINK_COUNTRY_MISMATCH are back to 0 because run_event_city_link quarantined the three mislinked events on its own at 03:05, and 99991790714809 cleared the one stale timezone that quarantine left behind. A zero-invariant gets repaired, never renegotiated. unlinked_venues: THIS IS THE COIN FLIP THE PREVIOUS REVISION PREDICTED IN WRITING -- it said `operations.unlinked_venues` carries the identical inflow defect as unlinked_events and 'is green only by luck, because it happens to be falling (3584 -> 3534 -> 3518)... it is the same coin flip the day that trend reverses'. It reversed. The drain is alive and proven: 8,715 of 12,051 gayout venues (72.3%) are already linked, wf_geo_link_content ran successfully minutes before this measurement at batch_limit 200, and the 3,336 outstanding are exactly the 09-28 batch. New ceiling = 6,827 currently unlinked + 3,336, the largest observed single-day unlinked-import burst, so one more gayout-sized import cannot red the repo. That is deliberately loose for a depth gauge, and the honest mitigation is named rather than assumed: A DEPTH CEILING IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT for a self-draining inflow queue, and this scorecard ALREADY has the right one -- `operations.image_automation_no_progress`, a drain-liveness boolean. Replacing both unlinked_* ceilings with a no-progress signal is the follow-up; until then a 3,000-venue producer regression could hide under this headroom, which is a worse trade than reddening every PR at random but is still a real cost. unlinked_events: 813 unlinked at measurement, +2 from 99991790714809's predecessor work leaving two correctly-unlinked events where two confidently-wrong links used to be (a null city_id is recoverable, a wrong one is not), + 36 = 90 days at the 0.4/day residue rate the previous revision measured. 851. THE REPAIR COMES FIRST THIS TIME, and it is 83% of the movement. The cities table has TRIPLED to 19,628 rows (CLAUDE.md still records ~5,700); 14,374 are `nominatim-geocode`, minted as a side effect of reverse-geocoding venue and event addresses. 16,175 were indexable and 5,633 of those carried no Wikidata identifier, which is what put CITY_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS 11x over.
